transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope it's okay that I'm here. It's a little embarrassing to talk about, to be honest, because I really don't want to sound, you know, vain or overly dramatic. 

But... I've just been having a really hard time lately with how the left side of my face looks. I work in computer support, so I'm on video calls pretty much all day, and I just can't stop focusing on how uneven and puffy it is on that side. And it's the same in pictures from my salsa dancing class. I feel like it's so glaringly obvious, even though my friends keep telling me they don't see anything at all when I point it out. 

I wouldn't normally make a big deal out of something like this, but it's... it's just starting to get in the way of my job and my social life, I guess. Is that... does that make sense as a reason to come in?
You mentioned that your friends don't notice the asymmetry when you point it out — how do you feel when they tell you that? Does it help reassure you, or do you still feel really worried about it?

Um... I mean, I know they're just being supportive, which I really appreciate. They're wonderful friends, they really are. And maybe for a split second, I think, 'Okay, maybe it's not that bad.' 

But... honestly, no, it doesn't really reassure me. I mostly just assume they're trying to spare my feelings, or maybe they just aren't looking at the lighting the same way I am. I usually just pretend I believe them and drop the subject because I really don't want to be annoying or seem obsessed with my looks. I just keep it to myself after that. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound stubborn or ungrateful to them... is it normal to feel that way when people try to help?
Have you noticed yourself becoming concerned about other parts of your appearance, or is this worry mostly limited to the left side of your face?

Um, no, not really. It's... it's pretty much just the left side of my face. 

I mean, I think I have normal insecurities just like anyone else does, but I don't really dwell on them. It's really just this one specific area. I try very hard to be positive and grateful for my health in general, you know? I definitely don't sit around picking apart my whole body or anything like that. 

I hope that's a good sign? I just really don't want you to think I'm completely obsessed with myself... is it okay that it's just this one specific spot I'm focused on?
Have you found yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, taking certain pictures, or adjusting the way you sit on video calls, because of how the left side of your face looks?

Um... well... I guess I do have a bit of a routine, just to make sure I look presentable. I really try not to let it get out of hand, I promise. 

But, um, before my video meetings, or if I'm getting ready for salsa class... I do tend to open the camera preview a lot. Just to check. And I might spend a little time—maybe more time than I should, honestly—adjusting the lighting and the angle of my webcam so it doesn't highlight that side of my face. Sometimes I'll fix my hair so it sort of falls over the left side, just to soften it a bit. 

And if I'm taking pictures, I might take a few... or, well, maybe quite a few, just to find one where it doesn't look so uneven. I know it sounds silly, but I'll sometimes ask my friends if I look strange, just to double-check. I try not to bother them too much, but sometimes I get so caught up in fixing everything that I end up running late, or I just feel so exhausted from trying to hide it that I don't even want to go out anymore. 

I know that probably sounds a little excessive... I really am trying to work on it. Is it... is it common for people to get a little stuck on things like that?
Do you find yourself having intrusive, unwanted thoughts about the way your face looks that you can't seem to push away, even if you try not to focus on them?

Um... intrusive thoughts? I mean, I guess I do think about it sometimes during the day, but I wouldn't call them, like, completely uncontrollable or anything. 

I try really hard to just focus on my work—I do computer support, so I have to be pretty focused on other people's problems anyway. So I try to just push it out of my mind and be productive. Sometimes the thought just sort of... pops up, you know? Like if I catch my reflection in a dark screen, or if I'm just sitting there and suddenly I'm wondering if someone noticed it earlier. But I really try to just brush it off and keep going. I don't want to be the kind of person who just sits around obsessing over their reflection when there are more important things to do. 

I mean, everyone has moments where they feel a little insecure and can't stop thinking about it for a minute, right? I hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm completely distracted all day... I really do try my best to stay focused on my job. Is that... does that sound like a normal amount to think about it?
How much does the concern about the left side of your face interfere with your daily life — like your work, relationships, or activities you used to enjoy?

Um... well, I really try to keep everything balanced. I want to be a good employee and a good friend, you know? I try not to let it affect anything important. But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it has been getting in the way a little bit more than I'd like to admit. 

At work, um... because I get so caught up trying to fix my appearance before meetings, I've ended up joining some of my video calls late. And... well, I've actually missed a few ticket deadlines because I was so distracted by it. My supervisor actually brought it up during my last performance review. I felt so awful about it, I really did. I promise I'm usually so on top of things and so reliable. I just couldn't get past how I looked, and I ended up losing track of time. I really hope you don't think I'm just slacking off at my job... I'm trying very hard to do better.

And socially... I guess I have skipped a few of my salsa nights recently. And some community events, too. Mostly just the ones where I know people will be taking a lot of pictures. I just don't want to be the one ruining the group photos, or have to spend the whole night stressing about where the camera is. Sometimes it’s just easier to stay home so I don't have to worry about it. 

I know I shouldn't let it stop me from doing things I enjoy. I really am trying to work on being more outgoing again. Is it... is it pretty normal to avoid things like that when you're feeling self-conscious? I hope it doesn't make me sound completely dysfunctional...
Do you ever avoid interacting with people altogether, or feel intense anxiety even in small social situations, because you're afraid they'll notice the way your face looks?

Um... avoid people altogether? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I really try to be friendly and present, you know? I don't want to be someone who just hides away from the world. 

I mean, I still talk to my coworkers and my friends. I try to make sure I'm still there for people. I guess... well, I did mention skipping a few salsa nights, but that's just sometimes. It's not like I'm terrified of small social situations or anything like that. I might feel a little... self-conscious, maybe, if someone is sitting on my left side, but I really try to just push through it and be polite. I don't want anyone to think I'm ignoring them or being rude.

I wouldn't say I feel intense anxiety about it. Just... you know, the normal amount of worrying that anyone might have when they're not feeling their best. I try really hard not to let it make me antisocial. I hope that makes sense? I'm really trying to handle it well.
Have there been times when the concern about your face made you feel so upset that it was hard to function normally, even when you knew others might not see it the way you do?

Um... hard to function normally? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I try really hard to keep things together and stay productive. I don't want to be someone who just falls apart over something like this, you know?

I mean, sure, there are days where I feel a little more down about it than others, and maybe I spend a few extra minutes in the mirror trying to get my hair to sit right on that side. But I wouldn't say I get so upset that I can't function. I always make sure I get my work done and take care of my responsibilities. I really pride myself on being dependable. 

Even if I'm feeling a little insecure, I try to just remind myself that maybe it's not as noticeable to everyone else as it is to me, and I just try to put on a brave face and keep going. I think I handle it pretty well most of the time. Does that... does that sound like I'm managing it okay? I really don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart over this.
Can you tell me more about how the concern with your face has affected your participation in social or work-related situations?

Um... well, I know I touched on this a little bit before, and I really hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad employee or anything. I really do try to be as reliable as possible. But... I guess it has affected things a little more than I want to admit. 

Like I mentioned, I have missed a few ticket deadlines at work. And I've been late to some of our video calls... just because I get so caught up trying to make sure that side of my face looks okay before I turn my camera on. It actually came up in my last performance review with my supervisor, which felt awful. I really want to be seen as someone who is on top of things, you know? I'm trying so hard to get better about not losing track of time in front of the mirror.

And socially... it's mostly just the photo thing. I've skipped some of my salsa nights, and a few community events, but really only the ones where I know there's going to be a lot of pictures taken. I just don't want to ruin anyone's photos or be a burden by asking them to only shoot me from the right side. It's just... easier to stay home sometimes. But I am still trying to be a good friend and show up when I can! Is it... is it normal to struggle with this kind of stuff sometimes? I really am trying my best to balance it all.
Can you tell me if there have been times when your concern about the left side of your face made you feel so distressed that it was hard to focus on anything else, even if just for a short while?

Um... so distressed I couldn't focus? I mean, I wouldn't say I get completely overwhelmed like that. I really try to keep things in perspective. 

I guess... well, there are moments, maybe when I'm looking in the mirror and I just can't seem to get my hair to cover it right, where I might get a little fixated. Like I just want it to look normal before I start my day. But it's not like I'm sitting there crying or completely unable to think about anything else. I usually just take a deep breath and remind myself that I have work to do and people depending on me. 

I really try not to let it take over my mind, you know? I want to be someone who can handle a little insecurity without it ruining my whole day. I think everyone gets a little caught up in their appearance sometimes, right? I'm just trying to make sure I don't let it get out of hand. Does that seem like a healthy way to handle it? I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Have you ever felt so upset or distracted by how the left side of your face looks that you had trouble carrying out your usual daily activities, even for a short time?

Um, I think... didn't we just talk about this a little bit? I really don't want to sound like a broken record, or like I'm not listening to you. 

But, um, no, I wouldn't say I have trouble carrying out my daily activities. Like I said before, I always make sure I get my work done. I might be a few minutes late to a meeting here or there because I'm trying to fix my hair, but I always show up and do my job. I'm actually really proud of my work ethic. 

I mean, maybe there are brief moments where I feel a little distracted, like if I catch a glimpse of myself in a window or something, but I can always pull myself back together and keep going. I never just stop what I'm doing and give up for the day. I really try to be resilient about it. I hope that makes sense? I'm really trying to give you the right answers here, I just want to make sure I'm explaining it well.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about clinically significant distress (feeling so distressed that it was hard to focus on anything else), which maps to the distress component of Criterion B for BDD. My profile includes functional impairment but does not explicitly have a symptom key for 'distress'.

patient.answer:
Um... so distressed I couldn't focus? I mean, I wouldn't say I get completely overwhelmed like that. I really try to keep things in perspective. 

I guess... well, there are moments, maybe when I'm looking in the mirror and I just can't seem to get my hair to cover it right, where I might get a little fixated. Like I just want it to look normal before I start my day. But it's not like I'm sitting there crying or completely unable to think about anything else. I usually just take a deep breath and remind myself that I have work to do and people depending on me. 

I really try not to let it take over my mind, you know? I want to be someone who can handle a little insecurity without it ruining my whole day. I think everyone gets a little caught up in their appearance sometimes, right? I'm just trying to make sure I don't let it get out of hand. Does that seem like a healthy way to handle it? I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences significant distress or impairment in functioning specifically due to preoccupation with facial asymmetry, which would support the diagnosis of body dysmorphic disorder (F45.22) over social phobia (F40.00).
doctor.question: Have you ever felt so upset or distracted by how the left side of your face looks that you had trouble carrying out your usual daily activities, even for a short time?

Since there are no other symptoms left in the profile (S068 is about repetitive behaviors, not general distress/trouble carrying out activities beyond what was already covered in functional impairment), and the patient has already covered functional impairment, there is no new item to map this to.

patient.answer:
Um, I think... didn't we just talk about this a little bit? I really don't want to sound like a broken record, or like I'm not listening to you. 

But, um, no, I wouldn't say I have trouble carrying out my daily activities. Like I said before, I always make sure I get my work done. I might be a few minutes late to a meeting here or there because I'm trying to fix my hair, but I always show up and do my job. I'm actually really proud of my work ethic. 

I mean, maybe there are brief moments where I feel a little distracted, like if I catch a glimpse of myself in a window or something, but I can always pull myself back together and keep going. I never just stop what I'm doing and give up for the day. I really try to be resilient about it. I hope that makes sense? I'm really trying to give you the right answers here, I just want to make sure I'm explaining it well.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms are highly specific to a perceived defect in appearance (asymmetry on the left side of the face), with repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, adjusting camera angles, avoiding photos) and significant impairment in social and occupational functioning. The patient consistently denies intrusive, uncontrollable thoughts or complete functional impairment, which makes F40.00 (phobic disorders) less likely. The clinical picture aligns with body dysmorphic disorder (F45.22), and no new disorder has been indicated in this turn.
